messages.content: Calculate the final temperature when 20 kg of water at 30 degree Celsius is mixed with 15 kg of water at 60 degree Celsius.

function.name: calculate_final_temperature
function.description: Calculates the final equilibrium temperature after mixing two bodies with different masses and temperatures Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

mass1.description: The mass of the first body (kg).

temperature1.description: The initial temperature of the first body (Celsius).

mass2.description: The mass of the second body (kg).

temperature2.description: The initial temperature of the second body (Celsius).

specific_heat_capacity.description: The specific heat capacity of the bodies in kJ/kg/K. If not provided, will default to that of water at room temperature, which is 4.2 kJ/kg/K. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning: We have a user request: "Calculate the final temperature when 20 kg of water at 30 degree Celsius is mixed with 15 kg of water at 60 degree Celsius." The user wants us to calculate the final temperature. We have a tool that calculates the final equilibrium temperature after mixing two bodies with different masses and temperatures. The user didn't provide the specific heat capacity, but we can use the default of 4.2 kJ/kg/K. The user didn't ask for the specific heat capacity. So we can call the tool with mass1=20, temperature1=30, mass2=15, temperature2=60. The user didn't specify the specific heat capacity, so we can omit it. The tool expects mass1, temperature1, mass2, temperature2, and optional specific_heat_capacity. So we can call the tool with mass1=20, temperature1=30, mass2=15, temperature2=60. That should produce the final temperature.
